Tomatoes (at least the ones I have experience with) only grow flowers on new flowering stalks - once they're done, they're done.

If you're single-stemming them and pinching out the suckers AND topping off the plant, you will eventually run out of flowering stalks.

You can re-root and plant the pinched-off suckers in another spot, and each will produce a new clone plant. I usually plant my indeterminate tomato seedlings out in April, and then re-plant a couple of suckers in June, to get a new start going while I harvest from the original. Zone 9b, so my growing season for tomatoes is all the way into early November. Your mileage may vary if you have a shorter season.
